_comment: The catalogue of German wind turbines, by generation. Dimensions are what
the Marktstammdatenregister says the fleet is (medians over three regions,
see crates/content/src/wind.rs) and what the manufacturers' data sheets say
the machines of that generation are built like.
One entry per size class: `hub_m` and `rotor_m` are what the model is built
at — the placement scales it to the machine that actually stands there.
`variants` lists the builds of that class: `standard` is the box nacelle
of Vestas, Nordex, Senvion, GE and Siemens, `enercon` the drop-shaped
nacelle and the green-graded tower foot of Enercon, `gitter` a lattice
tower (Fuhrländer, some Nordex and Tacke machines of the 1990s).
tower_base_m / tower_top_m: outside diameter of the tubular steel tower at
the ground and under the nacelle. rated_rpm: rotor speed at rated power,
read by the game off the rotor node's extras. blade: chord of the
cylindrical root, the widest chord and the tip [m]. nacelle: length (from
the hub back), width and height of the box [m]; the Enercon drop uses
length and diameter. overhang_m: hub centre in front of the tower axis.
marking: whether the machine's tip reaches over 100 m and therefore carries
the day marking (red/white/red blade tips, a red band on the tower) and the
night lights (Feuer W, rot) of the AVV Kennzeichnung.

classes.generation: 1990s: Enercon E-40, Vestas V44, Tacke TW 600, Nordex N43
2000s: Vestas V80, Enercon E-70, REpower MM82, Nordex N80, GE 1.5s
2010s: Enercon E-101, Vestas V112, Nordex N117, Senvion 3.2M114
2020s: Enercon E-138 EP3, Vestas V150, Nordex N149, Siemens Gamesa SG 5.8-155
